subject: URGENT: Variant surface rollout causing p95/p99 surge — triage + exec update
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara@venturametrics.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T23:18:00Z
Subject: Sudden p99/p95 spike after last night

Hi Aisha —

We started seeing major tail latency today around 22:30 PT, right after the rolling variant you mentioned was promoted. p95 jumped from ~210ms to ~1.2s and p99 is spiking above 3s. A bunch of our production queries time out (we're on the hosted API). Attaching a small sample of request IDs and HAR-like traces — the requests that time out all reference model_variant=v2.3.1 in the logs.

Example request ids: r-13f7, r-13f8, r-1402
Observed symptoms: high token generation latency, occasional 503s, and increased error-rate for longer inputs.

We are seeing customer impact (product search failing for some sessions). Can your team triage? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you can rollback the variant for us.

Thanks,
Sara
Senior SRE, Ventura Metrics
(attachment: ventura_sample_requests.json)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T23:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Sudden p99/p95 spike after last night — urgent triage request

Folks — forwarding an urgent customer report from Ventura Metrics. Internal triage requested. Key points:
- Trigger appears tied to the v2.3.1 model variant promoted in the staggered rollout at 22:00 PT.
- Symptoms: p95 ~1.2s, p99 >3s, some 503s.
- External sent a sample of failing request ids and traces (attached).

Immediate asks:
- Connor: can you look at serving/runtime metrics (KV cache hit rate, batching stats) for v2.3.1 and the affected zones?
- Priyom: please gather rollout timing and percent-of-traffic for Ventura's route (they were in the first 10% wave).
- Marissa: I need a short customer-facing mitigation plan (rollback vs routing pin) we can propose within 1 hour.

I will loop in infra/exec if this looks like a regression.

Thanks — Aisha
Product Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
(For visibility: attachment forwarded: ventura_sample_requests.json)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T00:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99/p95 spike after last night — initial triage notes

I'll keep this short — initial findings from the canary/variant telemetry:
- v2.3.1 shows a ~40% drop in KV cache hit rate for sequences >512 tokens (cluster us-west-2).
- Batch formation latency increased: median batch wait +35ms, which amplifies under mixed short/long request patterns for Ventura (they have many long prompts).
- We observed a kernel fallback on a subset of GPUs for v2.3.1 (FP16->FP32 path) for certain attention patterns — this is likely causing the CPU/GPU sync stalls and token-level tail latency.
- Error rate: 503 spikes align with bursty retry attempts after timeouts.

Immediate recommended mitigation:
1) Pin Ventura traffic to v2.3.0 (safe variant) for 100% of their route while we investigate — should be a config flip and can be done in ~10-15 minutes.
2) If pin is not feasible fast enough, do a regional rollback of v2.3.1 in us-west-2 for the affected pool.

I'll prepare a short diagnostic pack (logs + trace slice) and attach to the ticket.

Connor
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_trace_v2.3.1.log)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara@venturametrics.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T00:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden p99/p95 spike after last night — mitigation plan

Sara — thanks for the quick signal and for the sample traces. Short plan so we can get you stable ASAP:

What we'll do now (ETA ~15–30m):
- Immediate: Pin Ventura's route to v2.3.0 (Connor will flip). This avoids a full rollback and limits blast radius.
- Mitigation: We'll also temporarily apply a routing rule to prefer lower-latency hosts (burst capacity) while we root-cause.
- Compensation: We'll apply a service credit for impacted minutes during the incident window and follow up with a postmortem.

Could you confirm: is there any in-flight migration on your side that requires continuity to v2.3.1 specifically? If not, we'll proceed with pinning.

Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-12-10T00:58:00Z
Subject: Exec note: Ventura Metrics impact + recommended pin to v2.3.0

Markus — heads up: Ventura Metrics (strategic mid-market account, deal VM-3492) reported production degradation after our staggered rollout wave for variant v2.3.1. Connor's telemetry points to KV cache misses + a kernel fallback path for certain attention shapes leading to amplified token tail latency.

Recommended action we are executing now: pin Ventura traffic to v2.3.0 (to be applied in ~10m). If the pin does not stabilize, we will do a regional rollback in us-west-2. Marissa will communicate mitigation + credits to the customer.

I will keep you posted with progress and a follow-up postmortem link to JIRA-SUP-4568 once complete.

-Aisha

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T14:05:00Z
Subject: RESOLVED: Ventura Metrics p95/p99 surge — pin applied, metrics recovered

Update — final:
- At 13:45 PT we pinned Ventura to v2.3.0 and applied a routing preference to lower-latency hosts in us-west-2.
- Within three minutes p95 dropped back to ~230ms and p99 returned under 800ms. 503 rates returned to baseline.
- Root cause: an interaction between attention kernel path selection for v2.3.1 and our cache-key normalization for long sequences that produced cache churn and forced less efficient kernels.
- Next steps: Priyom will coordinate a targeted verification run for v2.3.1 with instrumented telemetry, Connor will prepare a regression fix and we will schedule a cautious canary re-run with smaller wave and extra observability.
- Postmortem: JIRA-SUP-4568 (will include timelines, metrics, and remediation).

Connor
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
